data.why: The dashboard reads candidate_ranking.csv, models/transit_classifier.pt, models/label_encoder.json, and data/processed/*.npz, all of which are already committed in the repository, so no additional data needs to be supplied.

goals: Review the trained Dual-View CNN's evaluation metrics (accuracy, ROC-AUC, precision, recall, F1) to judge model reliability before trusting its rankings
Browse the full prediction distribution and confidence histogram to understand how the model splits candidates between planet transits and false positives
Inspect the scientific priority ranking (confidence, SNR, transit depth, duration, orbital period) to identify the top candidates worth astronomical follow-up
Search and filter the sortable candidate table, then export the ranked list as CSV for offline analysis
Select an individual Kepler candidate in the Candidate Explorer to read its auto-generated plain-language explanation of why it was classified as it was
Examine a candidate's global (full folded) and local (zoomed) transit light curves to visually confirm the transit signal matches the model's prediction

review.summary: The tree matches the README's stated purpose and workflow closely: judge the model, rank and filter candidates, inspect one candidate's prediction, explanation and light curves, then export. It is well layered, and it records real problems such as the AUC mismatch, the score-scale mismatch and the contradictory explanation text. It needs small fixes before filing: two export claims are cited to screens that don't show a download, 'raw data views' is the wrong word, and the priority bar chart has no feature.
